source_text: Hoc nempe, quod dicitis multos et paucos, ad quantitatem infinitam pertinet, quoniam in comparatione mutua aut multitudo invenitur aut paucitas; conferens itaque Dominus multitudini pereuntium eos qui salvandi sunt, paucos eos vocavit; et hic Apostolus conferens his, qui ita peccassent ut Adam, illos, quos salvat Christi gratia, multo plures esse pronuntiat.
pass_a_gloss: This namely, that you say many and few, belongs to an infinite quantity, since in a mutual comparison either a multitude is found or a fewness; the Lord therefore, conferring those who are to be saved with the multitude of those perishing, called them few; and here the Apostle, conferring with those who had so sinned as Adam those whom the grace of Christ saves, pronounces them to be much more.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Surely your expressions ‘many’ and ‘few’ concern an unspecified quantity, since it is through mutual comparison that a number is found great or small. Comparing those to be saved with the multitude who perish, the Lord called them few. Here the apostle, comparing those whom Christ’s grace saves with those who had sinned as Adam did, declares them far more numerous (compare Matthew 7:13–14; Romans 5:15).

choices.why: In this book Julian usually means the Savior's gift abounding against Adam's sin (Rom 5), not later system-grace as a substance, and not 'favoritism' unless a suum-cuique definition is in play.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
